clue.text: Moment male is engaged by equality

clue.text: Check for flare-up, say, in international game

explanation.definitionFit: A test match is a game between national sides, chiefly in cricket and rugby, so it is an international fixture.

explanation.definitionFit: A matinee is an afternoon performance of a play or screening of a film, so it is a film showing.

clue.text: Piano organ finally fixed by qualified person

explanation.definitionFit: A grand is the large concert piano with a horizontal frame, so the noun stands for the instrument.

clue.text: Entrance two audiences

explanation.surface: A doorway that lets in two separate crowds.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are words for an audience: the gate at a football ground and the house at a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A gatehouse is the building at the gate of an estate or castle, where people enter, so it serves as an entrance.

clue.text: Aberration, as expected, not right to appear within a year

indicators.note: the shortened word appears within the pair of letters, placed in their middle
not right means without the right letter, so that letter is removed

parts.note: normal means as expected or usual

explanation.walkthrough: 'as expected' looks like a comment on the aberration, but it is the wordplay's first ingredient; 'not' and 'to appear within' then act on it.
explanation.definitionFit: An anomaly is something deviating from what is standard or expected, which is what an aberration is.

clue.text: Criticise Irish county's change of heart, bringing in Conservative

explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of DERRY is its central R, which becomes C.
explanation.definitionFit: To decry something is to denounce it publicly, a stronger synonym of criticise.

clue.text: Original founder of sports venue from Land's End?

parts.note: the word land supplies its first letter, one of its two ends

explanation.surface: Asking whether the man behind a famous ground came from the tip of Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: Land's End is Cornwall's westernmost point, but here it is the ends of the word 'land': L or D, written out in full as L-OR-D. Thomas Lord founded Lord's, the London cricket ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Lord, a cricketer and businessman, established the ground that bears his surname, so his name defines its original founder.

clue.text: Bound to accept source of personal documentation with unknown clarity

explanation.definitionFit: Limpidity is the quality of being limpid, perfectly clear, whether of water or of prose, so it means clarity.

clue.text: Came to a point when cycling progress is slowed by this

explanation.walkthrough: Move the last three letters of TAPERED to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Red tape is excessive bureaucratic procedure, which slows down getting things done.

clue.text: TV show depicting you in a domestic context, ultimately going wild

parts.note: taken as written as anagram material

indicators.note: ultimately takes the closing letter of the word context

explanation.definitionFit: A sitcom is a television series whose humour comes from recurring characters in everyday settings, so it is a kind of TV show.

clue.text: A great deal, securing backing of fashionable European city

indicators.note: the word for a great deal secures, or holds firm inside it, the reversed letters

indicators.note: the backing of a word reads it from the back, so the letters for fashionable are turned round

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'

explanation.surface: A big business deal to secure backing from a stylish European city.
explanation.definitionFit: Munich is the capital of Bavaria in southern Germany, a major city of the continent.

clue.text: Play with Act I junked? That's not usual

parts.note: taken as written as anagram material
taken as written as anagram material

explanation.definitionFit: Atypical describes something that departs from the norm or the expected type, so it is what is not usual.

clue.text: Government department attempt to secure unlimited quantity

indicators.note: the word for attempt holds the other letters securely inside itself

parts.note: a measure is a set quantity, as of a drink

explanation.definitionFit: The Treasury is the UK ministry that manages public finances and economic policy, a department of government.

clue.text: Single recipient? Also include most of the others, do you understand?

parts.note: to add is to include as well

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its final letter

parts.note: the rest are the others
see? means do you understand?

explanation.surface: Someone checking whether the rest of a mailing list should be copied in.
explanation.definitionFit: An addressee is the person to whom a letter is directed, so one receiver of it.

clue.text: Made ready? Something like 29 pence!

parts.note: 29 is a prime number, so something like it is a prime
d was the abbreviation for pence in pre-decimal British money

explanation.surface: Asking whether 29p is enough to make things ready, exclaimed like a price tag.
explanation.walkthrough: Before 1971 British pennies were written d (from the Latin denarius), so D stands for pence.
explanation.definitionFit: To prime something is to prepare it for use, as with a pump or a surface before painting, so primed means prepared.

clue.text: Restrict slight cut applied to a coastal region

parts.note: to pen is to confine or restrict

indicators.note: cut means trimmed, losing its last letter

parts.note: a slight is an insult

explanation.surface: Imposing limits and a small trim on an area by the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A peninsula is land almost surrounded by water, projecting into the sea, so it is a region on the coast.

clue.text: Enjoyed course covering revolutionary paintings and English lit

indicators.note: the meal word covers the other letters by wrapping round them

parts.note: dined means ate a meal, enjoyed a course

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: art means paintings

explanation.surface: A literature student who had a fine time on a course of radical art and English literature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lit' looks like literature after 'English', but it is the verb, past tense of alight: getting off a train.
explanation.definitionFit: To detrain is to get off a train, and alight has the past form lit, so detrained means alighted.

clue.text: Tackle limitations to habitual energy

clue.text: A problematic situation between Democrat and Republican, one fancies

explanation.definitionFit: An admirer is someone attracted to another person, so the noun phrase is fitted by a person who fancies someone.

clue.text: Love lots of money — it attracts people

explanation.definitionFit: A honeypot is a place or thing that draws crowds, like bees to honey, so it attracts people.

explanation.definitionFit: A panacea is a supposed remedy for every disease or problem, a universal cure.

clue.text: Threatening to offload indefinite number, causing obstruction

explanation.definitionFit: Impeding means hindering or blocking progress, so it is the act of causing an obstruction.

clue.text: Obsessed with stifling rook opening

indicators.note: stifling smothers the letter by surrounding it

parts.note: into means keen on or obsessed with
R is the chess notation for rook

clue.text: Take decisive step when appealing to accommodate dodgy sorts in advance

parts.note: taken as written as anagram material

clue.text: Unrestrained shift in Fahrenheit affecting diving venue?

clue.text: Experienced receiving first instalment of National Assistance
